concern: (low) Navigation anchor references (#section-0, #section-1, #section-2) use generic placeholder fragment identifiers that should link to concrete route landmarks in final integration.
jtbd: When navigating the interface via the header menu, I want anchor links to point to semantic, meaningful landmarks on the page, so that I can reliably orient myself and jump to relevant sections without encountering dead ends or cryptic IDs.
acceptanceCriteria: Given the header navigation element, When inspecting the href attributes of all anchor links, Then they reference existing semantic section IDs (e.g. #hero-heading / #overview, #telemetry-heading / #telemetry, #form-heading / #control-parameters) matching landmark sections in the DOM rather than generic #section-N placeholders.
editInstruction: In the header navigation (<nav role="navigation">), replace href="#section-0" with href="#hero-heading" (or add id="overview" to the hero section and link to #overview), replace href="#section-1" with href="#telemetry-heading" (or link to #telemetry with matching section id), and replace href="#section-2" with href="#form-heading" (or matching id on control parameters section).

concern: (low) Control parameter form inputs could provide aria-describedby helper annotations to further optimize cognitive ease for screen reader users.
jtbd: When filling out the control parameter form using assistive technologies, I want form fields to explicitly reference helper explanations via aria-describedby, so that I understand expected formats and parameter constraints without cognitive friction or trial-and-error.
acceptanceCriteria: Given the control parameters form inputs (#user-email and #project-archetype-select), When a screen reader focuses on each field, Then it announces associated description text referenced via aria-describedby pointing to visible helper text elements with unique matching IDs.
